rationale: THE RECEIVER-TYPE SPELLING, pinned with its boundaries. A bare member whose receiver's type the run cannot see used to drop the owner and keep the leaf; the census priced the spelling (`Type.member`) against the gate's own key space — on riverpod's calls 966 ambiguous rows resolve while 129 resolved rows stop being resolvable, and the rest stay honestly unresolved — so the row is now spelled and the claim that makes it honest is attached: `baseBeyondRunScope: <type>`, the declared cause whose contract is 'the run that wrote this edge could not look the owner up'. It can never raise a resolution (the gate reads it only where the target names NOTHING) and its reason is checked against the edge's own target owner. Four boundaries are pinned because a spelling that fires one case too widely moves thousands of corpus rows silently: (C) a LOWERCASE head names no type, so no spelling exists and the old decline must stay exactly as it was; (D) a type visible in the file that declares the member keeps resolving through the visible-type path, with NO claim; (F) a type visible in the file that does NOT declare the member keeps `receiverMemberOutsideRun` and its bare target — the project cannot declare `Bare.missingMember`, because `Bare` is declared here without it. THE CLAIM MUST ALSO SURVIVE THE METADATA TERNARIES: the first application of this change dropped it at three sites whose metadata was written `q.target ? {qualifier: …} : {…receiverCut(q)}`, and the `uses` read of `args.first` came out spelled with NO marker — a spelling whose non-resolution the gate would charge to the lane. The dump caught it, not the reading, which is why case C's `List.first` row is pinned with both its qualifier AND its claim.

expectRelationships.note: case A — a CAPITALIZED head whose type this file does not declare. The target names the type instead of the bare leaf `make`, and the claim names the owner the run could not look up. `receiverCause: null` pins the mutual exclusion: a spelled row carries the CLAIM, never a cut cause.
case B, first half — the constructor call itself is spelled by the same branch

case B, the row this class exists for — `ext.frob()` where `ext` is a local with an EXPLICIT type. The site writes a value and the run still knows the type name, which is why `receiverTypeOutsideRun` was never only about capitalized literals
the local read is a BINDING and is untouched by the spelling — its target is already unspeakable as a declaration

case C, the lower boundary — `args.first` names no type, so the head stays a VALUE, the target stays the bare leaf, and the cut still reports `receiverTypeUnknown`. `baseBeyondRunScope: null` is the pin that catches a spelling that overruns: if the branch ever fires here, this row gains a claim and the check fails.

the row that caught the dropped claim: `args` is typed `List<dynamic>`, the head's type resolves to `List`, the target is spelled — and the claim MUST ride with it, or a row the project cannot resolve reads as an unmarked gap. Both the qualifier and the claim are pinned, because the two ternaries that write them were the defect

case E — an SDK type (implicit `dart:core`). The spelling fires and the claim is what keeps the row honest: `String` is outside every project this corpus holds, so no index of the project could ever have resolved it

case D, the upper control — the declaring type is in this file, the enclosing-class rule resolves the call, and the new branch must not touch it. `baseBeyondRunScope: null` is the assertion that the spelling did not spread to rows the analyzer already answered

case F — the type IS visible here and does not declare the member, so the declaring type is elsewhere. Deliberately NOT spelled this round: the project cannot declare `Bare.missingMember` because `Bare` is declared here without it, so a spelling would convert an ambiguity into a certain non-resolution

forbidRelationships.note: the OLD bare shape, pinned as forbidden: the whole point of the change is that `ExternalThing.make` replaces `make`, and the bare form would be an ambiguous leaf again
case C, negative side — the bare leaf must not survive beside the spelling

case C, THE BOUNDARY — a lowercase head names no type, so this spelling must NOT exist. A branch that fell back to the local's own name (the pre-cut behaviour the fixture `receiver-cause` already refuted once) would produce exactly this row
case D — the resolved call must not also appear bare

expectRelationshipCount.note: four spelled (A, B's two, E) + one enclosing (D) + two declined (C, F)
one spelled member read (`List.first`) + five bindings
